title: Magneto retrofit benchmark: queue-oscillation and cost-stability playbook
summary: POC benchmark of integrating Redwood inference into Magneto's existing synchronous checkout recommendation path. Focus on queue oscillation effects under mixed-size requests and recommended runtime settings to hit 99th/99.9th latency targets without >20% cost increase.
content:
Executive summary:

This benchmark evaluates a Magneto POC deployment pattern where Redwood inference is retrofitted into a synchronous checkout RPC used for final product recommendations (latency SLO target: p99 < 250 ms). Magneto's production mixes short single-item prompts (avg tokens 18) and longer contextual prompts (avg tokens 140) at a 7:1 ratio. We focused on how request queueing and autoscaling behavior interact with batching/caching and quantized models to affect tail latency and unit cost.

Key takeaways:
- Baseline (no KV cache, continuous batching enabled at default throughput settings) achieved p50=34ms, p95=112ms, p99=320ms, p99.9=890ms on RW-7B-v1 (fp16) at 300 QPS. p99 exceeded Magneto's 250 ms SLO in steady state due to intermittent queue oscillations when bursts arrive.
- Switching to RW-7B-q4_0 (quantized int4) reduced median/mean token compute and lowered p99 to 220ms, p99.9 to 560ms, but increased token generation variance for long prompts (occasional 2x decoding stalls) requiring tuning of kernel fallback thresholds.
- Enabling prefix KV caching for repeat session contexts (simulated 32% cache-hit rate) reduced CPU/KV read overhead and trimmed p95 by ~18% and p99 by ~23%. Effective for Magneto's repeat-customer flows.
- Autoscaling policy changes (faster scale-up, conservative scale-down) smoothed queue drain and reduced microburst-induced p99.9 spikes by 60% at a modest cost uplift (~6% monthly).
- Cost profile: using RW-7B-q4_0 with caching and adjusted autoscaler produced a projected token cost reduction of ~28% vs baseline fp16 at matched p95, and an overall per-100k-request platform cost (in this POC config) of $41.2.

Goals and success criteria:
- Achieve p99 < 250 ms for the mixed workload in steady state and under 2x baseline burst loads for 95% of test windows.
- Keep total platform cost increase under 15% relative to Magneto's current hybrid CPU-based inference solution for parity feature set.
- Produce a clear operations playbook (autoscaler + batching + model selection) that Magneto SRE can own.

Testbed and methodology:
- Hardware: Dedicated Redwood instance on H100-80GB (single-GPU slots used to reflect Magneto Dedicated sizing) and an alternative configuration on A100-40GB for comparison runs.
- Models tested: RW-7B-v1 (fp16), RW-7B-q4_0 (quantized int4), RW-13B-q4_0 (quantized int4 - for headroom checks).
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime v1.9.2 (with experimental kernel fallback enabled for q4 paths).
- Workload generation: replay of Magneto anonymized production traces (7:1 short:long request ratio) with synthetic 3x burst windows every 5 minutes to exercise autoscaling and queue dynamics.
- Metrics captured: latency distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9), request QPS, GPU utilization, average tokens per request, cold-start fraction, KV-cache hit rate, and per-minute cost counters (estimated compute + inferencing overhead).
- Windows: steady-state (30 min), burst stress (10 min bursts with up to 3x QPS), and long-tail soak (2 hours at 1.5x baseline).

Detailed results (selected):
1) Baseline (RW-7B-v1 fp16), continuous batching default settings, no KV cache, autoscaler policy: scale-up trigger 70% GPU, scale-down delay 60s:
- Steady state (300 QPS): p50=34ms, p90=85ms, p95=112ms, p99=320ms, p99.9=890ms. GPU util 62% avg.
- Burst window (900 QPS sustained 30s): p99 jumps to 1.8s, p99.9 to 3.6s due to queuing and slow scale-up.
- Cost proxy: baseline per-100k requests = $56.8 (includes reserved infra amortized).

2) Quantized (RW-7B-q4_0), same runtime, no cache, default autoscaler:
- Steady state: p50=28ms, p95=95ms, p99=220ms, p99.9=560ms. GPU util 78% avg.
- Burst: p99 0.95s, p99.9 1.9s. Some decoding stalls observed at 0.7% of long requests; traced to kernel fallback when sequence length crosses 256 tokens and fallback to slower kernels occurred.
- Cost proxy: per-100k requests = $40.9 (quantization compute savings).

3) Quantized + KV prefix cache (simulated 32% hit), autoscaler tuned (scale-up threshold 55%, aggressive scale-up window 15s, conservative scale-down 120s):
- Steady state: p50=25ms, p95=78ms, p99=170ms, p99.9=220ms. GPU util 68% (lower tail variance).
- Burst: p99 0.45s, p99.9 0.9s. Queue oscillation significantly damped due to faster scale-up and longer drain windows.
- Cost proxy: per-100k requests = $41.2 (overall monthly infra cost ~6% higher than raw quantized baseline but far superior p99 profile).

4) RW-13B-q4_0 (safety check for headroom):
- Steady state: p95=190ms, p99=410ms. Cost per-100k requests = $92. Estimated headroom available but not cost-effective for this latency-targeted, short-prompt-dominated workload.

Observations and root causes:
- Queue oscillation: primary contributor to p99/p99.9 spikes is autoscaler hysteresis combined with mixed request sizes. When burst arrives, batching briefly increases queue depth to amortize tokens, then scale-up happens and batch size reduces, causing an undershoot/overshoot oscillation that amplifies tail latency for a few minutes per burst.
- Quantization behavior: q4 provides strong median improvements but has kernel edge-cases at >256 token sequences that force slower pathways; this appears as a small fraction of long requests with doubled latency.
- Cache effectiveness: Magneto's repeat-contexts are highly cacheable; even a 25-35% hit rate materially reduces p95/p99 and lowers GPU pressure, improving scaling dynamics.
- Cost tradeoffs: small infra policy adjustments (faster scale-up, longer scale-down) increase infra hours modestly but produce large tail-latency improvements. Quantization buys most of the unit-cost savings.

Recommendations (actionable runbook):
1) Model selection: use RW-7B-q4_0 as primary model for the checkout path. Reserve RW-13B-q4_0 for multi-turn upsell/creative flows where quality is required.
2) Autoscaler config (recommended): scale-up when GPU util >55% sustained 10-15s, scale-down only after 90-120s of below-threshold utilization. Set burst-provisioning headroom to 30% for the checkout route.
3) Batching: enable continuous micro-batching with a max coalesce latency of 10ms and a hard max batch size tuned to 512 tokens. Prioritize shorter prompts for lower-latency paths (route long prompts to a background pool with larger batch sizes).
4) KV caching: enable prefix cache with a warmed-out policy for logged-in customers. Target cache-hit >=30% for the checkout flow via session keying. Implement cache metrics and alert when hit rate falls below 20%.
5) Kernel fallback tuning: adjust the q4 fallback threshold to favor the optimized kernels for sequences up to 384 tokens where empirical stall is low; monitor the 95th percentile decode time for long prompts and revert if stalls increase.
6) Canary + rollout plan: staged canary starting at 1% traffic on RW-7B-q4_0 + cache enabled -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with real-time p95/p99 dashboards and automatic rollback on p99 > 300ms for 5 consecutive minutes.

Suggested telemetry and alerts:
- Per-route p50/p95/p99/p99.9 (1m and 5m windows).
- Queue depth and average batch size per GPU (1m).
- KV cache hit rate and bytes served (1m).
- Kernel fallback counts (per-minute).
- Autoscaler scale events and time-to-scale metrics.
- Alert if p99 > 300ms for 3 consecutive minutes or if kernel fallback rate >0.5% sustained for 5 minutes.

Open risks and follow-ups:
- Long-prompt stalls: investigate kernel fusion options and additional q8 prototypes with Redwood research to remove the 2x decode stalls seen in ~0.7% of long requests.
- Mixed fleet behavior: Magneto runs a multi-region setup; multi-region routing and cross-region warm caches need a small coordination project to avoid cold-cache penalties.
- Cost baseline accuracy: platform cost proxies used here are POC estimates; final contract pricing for Dedicated slots and sustained usage discounts will materially change per-100k numbers. Confirm with finance for final proposal.

Appendix A — Raw sample windows (selected extracts):
- Raw log snippet (burst window): time=2029-11-11T14:03:12Z qps=880 batch_mean=18 batch_max=512 p99=1.82s scale_event=start_up -> 3 GPUs in 28s
- Kernel fallback record: request_id=abc-43397 sequence_len=312 fallback=true delta_ms=1213

Appendix B — Minimal magneto ops checklist for Phase 1 rollout:
- Instrument route-level traces and expose resource metrics to Magneto monitoring (Prometheus export).
- Provision KV cache namespace and TTLs, seed with top-100 shopper sessions for warmup test.
- Configure autoscaler as recommended and run 48-hour soak at 1.2x baseline before 5% canary.
- Schedule engineering runbook review with Magneto SRE for operational run scenarios (coldstart, db outage, region failover).

Next steps:
- Internal: Solutions-eng to produce a compact canary runbook (2 pages) and a 1-hour SRE workshop with Magneto to walk through failover and rollback. (Owners: Daniel Kim, Aisha Navarro).
- Customer: propose a 6-week Phase 1 plan that includes cache rollout, autoscaler tuning, and a 2-week production canary. Estimated uplift in subscription/infra cost for Phase 1: +8% (to be finalized).
